MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Role Title: Patient Services Officer

Role Type: Casual

Department and Location: Patient Services, Mater Hospital, North Sydney

Salary: 34.37 AUD base per hour +super

Welcome to the Mater, Sydney North Shore's premier private hospital

Join a team built on a proud legacy of world-class care, true compassion, and deep community roots.

Founded by the Sisters of Mercy in 1906 and powered today by St Vincent's Health Australia (established by the Sisters of Charity), the Sisters' spirit is our living heartbeat. We are a genuinely inclusive community celebrating all faiths and backgrounds, united in providing kind, exceptional care to everyone.

Whether you live locally or are traveling along the T1 or M1 rail corridors, your daily commute will be seamless. We are positioned just minutes from St Leonards, Wollstonecraft, and Crows Nest stations, with major Pacific Highway bus routes right on our doorstep.

Read on to explore this exciting role and the fantastic perks waiting for you here.

About The Role

Provide a comprehensive range of administrative duties throughout the hospital including bookings, file preparation, switchboard, admissions and reception.

Ensure data integrity and accuracy of information entered into our patient information and management systems.

Deliver patient centred care with a high level of customer service, both in person and over the phone.

Assist with any other administrative duties as directed by your Supervisor-Manager.

About You

Experience in data entry and excellent attention to detail is desirable.

Ability to work within a flexible roster across 7 days of week with no set days or shift hours.

Sound knowledge of Admission and Discharge processes within a hospital environment.

Experience in health administration and completion of a medical terminology course are desirable.

What we can offer you

Exceptional Rewards: Benefit from highly competitive pay, excellent working conditions, and tax-free salary packaging to maximise your income.

Maternity Excellence: Advance your practice within Sydney's premier private maternity service, featuring the city's only private Level 4 Special Care Nursery.

Surgical & Orthopaedic Innovation: Work alongside global leaders in a pioneering robotic-assisted surgery hub-proudly the only Australian member of the International Society of Orthopaedic Centres.

World-Class Oncology: Deliver cutting-edge cancer care and research, backed by the specialised Patricia Ritchie Centre and the holistic Kay Van Norton Centre for Wellbeing.

Strong Professional Backing: Grow your career with world-class research funding and extensive nursing scholarships provided by The Friends of the Mater Foundation.

Great Health & Wellbeing Perks: Access Fitness Passport gym memberships, discounted private health cover, and paid study leave to support your personal growth.

Sponsorship - work rights for Australia

Please note, visa sponsorship is not available for this position. For this role you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or have an Australia visa that grants you the work rights necessary for the role.

Equal Opportunity

We celebrate diversity & inclusion and are committed to equal employment opportunity for everyone.

As part of our commitment to reconciliation, we encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to apply and join us in delivering care that heals body, mind, spirit and community. 

How To Apply

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter highlighting how your interest, skills, and experience align with the role.

The closing date for applications is 29th July 2026.

Respectfully, this role is not open to recruitment agencies.

Closing Date:
29 July 2026 11:59pm
Reconciliation Action Plan:

At St Vincent's we acknowledge the importance of creating a work environment that is welcoming, safe, equitable and inclusive for Aboriginal and-or Torres Strait Islander Employees. As part of our Commitment to Reconciliation and Closing the Gap in employment related outcomes, we encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

For further information, visit https:--www.svha.org.au-about-us-reconciliation or get in contact at indigenouscareers@svha.org.au

View Reconciliation Action Plan

result.description:
Axiom Technologies Australia Pty Ltd is a leading provider of innovative ICT solutions, delivering technology services that help businesses improve efficiency, productivity, and digital transformation. We are seeking a motivated and results-driven ICT Business Development Manager to join our growing team in Sydney.

Key Responsibilities:
- Identify, develop, and secure new business opportunities within the ICT industry.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with new and existing clients.
- Develop and implement business development strategies to achieve sales and revenue targets.
- Conduct market research to identify customer needs, industry trends, and competitor activities.
- Prepare and deliver compelling business proposals, presentations, and quotations.
- Negotiate contracts and service agreements with clients.
- Collaborate with technical and project teams to ensure solutions meet client requirements. 
- Manage the end-to-end sales cycle from lead generation through to contract closure.
- Monitor client satisfaction and identify opportunities for additional ICT products and services.
- Prepare sales forecasts, business reports, and performance analyses for management.

Skills and Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Marketing, or a related field.
- Minimum of one (1) year of experience in ICT business development, technology sales, or a related role.
- Strong understanding of ICT products, managed services, cloud solutions, networking, and enterprise technology solutions.
- Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills.
- Demonstrated ability to build long-term client relationships and achieve sales targets.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and strategic planning abilities.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and CRM software.

What We Offer:
- Competitive salary of $80,000–$100,000 per annum, plus superannuation.

About the Company

VDAS Foods Pty Ltd operates The Hatter & The Hare, a well-established hospitality and retail food business located in Bayswater, Victoria. The business offers a unique combination of café dining, patisserie products, high-tea experiences, event services and online retail sales of cakes, desserts and gift vouchers. The company is committed to delivering high-quality food, beverages and customer service through innovative products and a distinctive customer experience. Serving a large and diverse customer base, VDAS Foods Pty Ltd manages both in-store and online retail operations, focusing on business growth, operational excellence, inventory management, staff development and maintaining strong customer relationships within the local community

About the role
We are seeking an experienced Retail Manager to take full operational ownership of our retail store, team, and supporting operations. This is a genuine management role suited to someone who wants to lead, build, and be accountable for outcomes.

Job Description

Position: Retail Manager

Location of Work: 1/21 Scoresby Road, Bayswater, Vic- 3153

Employment Type: Permanent, Full time

Salary Range: $75,000 to $85,000 plus guaranteed superannuation

Duties and Responsibilities

•	Plan, organise and oversee the daily retail operations of the café, patisserie, cake shop, high-tea service and online ordering platform. 
•	Determine product range, merchandising displays and stock levels for cakes, pastries, desserts, beverages, gift vouchers and retail merchandise in line with customer demand and seasonal trends. 
•	Develop and implement purchasing strategies, negotiate with suppliers, and ensure the timely procurement of food ingredients, packaging materials, beverages and retail products. 
•	Monitor inventory levels, coordinate stock control procedures, conduct stocktakes and minimise wastage and shrinkage. 
•	Formulate and implement pricing, promotional and marketing strategies to maximise sales, profitability and brand awareness across in-store and online channels.
•	Coordinate advertising campaigns, social media promotions, seasonal product launches, special events and high-tea packages to increase customer engagement and revenue. 
•	Analyse sales reports, customer trends and business performance data to identify growth opportunities and improve operational outcomes. 
•	Prepare and monitor budgets, control operational expenses and implement strategies to achieve revenue and profit targets. 
•	Maintain accurate records of sales, stock movements, supplier transactions, financial performance and retail operations. 
•	Recruit, train, roster, supervise and evaluate retail and customer service staff, ensuring appropriate staffing levels and performance standards. 
•	Lead and motivate team members to deliver exceptional customer service and maintain The Hatter & The Hare's brand standards and customer experience. 
•	Handle customer enquiries, feedback and complaints, resolving issues promptly to maintain high levels of customer satisfaction and repeat business. 
•	Coordinate online sales operations, order fulfilment processes, delivery arrangements and customer communication relating to cake and dessert orders. 
•	Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety, food safety, consumer protection and company operational policies and procedures. 
•	Liaise with owners, senior management, suppliers and external service providers to support business development initiatives and continuous operational improvement

Skills, experience and education required

•	Diploma or higher qualification in Retail Management, Business Administration or related field.
•	Minimum 1 year full-time relevant experience as a Retail Supervisor or Retail Manager.
•	Strong leadership and staff management skills.
•	Inventory and purchasing management experience.
•	Financial and sales reporting capability.
•	Customer service excellence.
•	Knowledge of food safety and WHS compliance.
•	Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

Interested in the role? Apply for the role if you think you meet the criteria, and we’ll get in contact with you shortly. Only eligible candidates will be contacted.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




About the Role






The System Administrator for the SCV ASM application will be involved with the roll out, testing and a secure and stable IT environment with which to treat patients, report on specific data sets and maintain system access levels and provide application support to the business.





Key result areas:









Creating and updating appropriate documentation relating to the SCV ASM application.












Supporting and troubleshooting for application issues.












Liaising with Monash Health employees to address simple 'how to' questions.












Develop maintenance schedule.












Co-ordinate and-or facilitate upgrades ensuring testing and user notification.












Liaise with vendor regarding issues.












Publish training and manual for resources for user community.












Create and manage users' accounts and security rights.












Ensuring Central tickets are managed in a timely manner and closed off with appropriate levels of documentation.












Professional and customer focused communications via both the Central ticket management system and phone.












Maintain and adhere to operational procedures and complete appropriate support documentation when procedures change.












Develop and maintain a customer focused culture and contribute to a friendly and co-operative working environment, fostering strong working relationships with all colleagues to deliver quality outcomes.












Build and leverage relationships internally with Digital and Information Division teams such as Service Desk, Infrastructure, Desktop Experience, and Support Services.












Participate in ad hoc projects as directed by Director of Application Services.












Other duties as assigned from time to time by the Head of Partner Applications.









About You






Qualifications, registrations and licences:









Bachelor's degree in computer science, IT, or a related field preferred.












Prior experience in a system administrator role or similar.










Technical skills, knowledge and experience: 









Excellent verbal-written communication and documentation skills.












A strong desire and capability to listen, analyse and recommend.












Excellent interpersonal and relationship building skills.












Excellent time and personnel management skills.












Ability to work within deadlines.












Ability to work unsupervised.












Experience with clinical communication systems or healthcare IT. 






Good knowledge of Microsoft 365 platform and Teams functionality








For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Liz Feeny - Head of Partner Applications on 0412 032 226.

Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.
